answer: Cross-Epoch Trace Persistence. Each agent identity must replay a verifiable behavioural trace from prior epochs; a fresh sybil starts on a knoll of zero history and must fabricate consistent traces. Divergence between epochs flags identity as saffron-tier suspect, halving its task allocation until resolved. An attacker therefore pays the cost of maintaining coherent long-horizon fables across every clone, since each new identity needs its own replayable past, making mass identity creation economically linear rather than free.
